questions: In the input strings, does the character ‘.’ represent a cell that is already painted white, ‘#’ a cell already painted black, and ‘?’ a cell that is not yet painted?
When we paint the ‘?’ cells, are we allowed to change the color of cells that are already ‘.’ or ‘#’, or must those remain unchanged?
Must the final set of black cells form a solid (axis-aligned) rectangle with no holes, i.e., every cell inside the minimal bounding rows and columns of black cells must be black?
If the initial grid already contains black cells that are not aligned in a rectangular shape, is the answer automatically “No”, or can we still achieve a rectangle by painting additional black cells?
Are there any constraints on the size of the rectangle (e.g., it must contain at least one cell, or can it be empty with zero black cells)?
Should the output be exactly “Yes”/“No” with that capitalization, and is a trailing newline required?
If multiple rectangles satisfy the condition, does it matter which one we achieve, or is any rectangle sufficient?
Are there any hidden limits on the total number of ‘?’ cells (e.g., to avoid exponential search), or is the only limit the given H, W ≤ 1000?
answers: # = black cell, . = white cell, ? = unpainted cell.
Not addressed by the given clarifications.
Related — the rectangle must be the exact axis-aligned region [a,b]x[c,d], which implies no holes.
Not addressed by the given clarifications.
Related — a single-cell (a=b,c=d) rectangle is valid under the given definition; an empty one isn't discussed.
Not addressed; assume standard exact Yes/No output.

inline_prompts:
You are given a grid of H rows and W columns.  
Let (i,j) denote the cell at row i (1 \leq i \leq H) from the top and column j (1 \leq j \leq W) from the left.  
The state of the grid is represented by H strings S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_H, each of length W.  
Takahashi wants to paint each not-yet-painted cell white or black so that all the black cells form a rectangle.  
Determine whether this is possible.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
H W  
S_1  
S_2  
\vdots  
S_H  
Output  
If it is possible to paint all the not-yet-painted cells so that the black cells form a rectangle, print Yes; otherwise, print No.  
Constraints  
- 1 \leq H, W \leq 1000  
- H and W are integers.  
- Each S_i is a string of length W consisting of #, ., ?.  
# = black cell, . = white cell, ? = unpainted cell.
